What the data forced

Four results that changed the model.

Each of these cost real time to establish and each one is load-bearing — change the scope without accounting for them and the output is silently wrong.

67.4%vs 38.8%

Dormancy is a spread, not a number

Federal IT product codes migrated from the numeric 70-series to the alphanumeric 7A–7K family in a single step at the FY2020/21 boundary. A code set drawn from one era alone shows accounts going dormant as a pure artifact of recoding. Every family spans both eras, and every award carries its coding era.

51.9%baseline 77.4%

The channel rule is worse than no rule

Classifying vendors from NAICS and name scores below always guessing the majority class. NAICS on a federal award describes what was bought, not what the vendor is: 82,901 awards carry “Electronic Computer Manufacturing” because a computer was purchased. Production uses the SAM registration flag; the rule is reported, not used.

0.802baseline 0.697

The headline AUC is flattered

Across all 3,043 test accounts the model reaches 0.922 — but most of that lift is separating long-dead accounts from live ones, which needs no model. On the 1,229 recently-active accounts, where the ranking actually operates, it scores 0.802 against a 0.697 baseline. That is the number worth quoting.

153,911from 270,924

Model the purchase episode

Time between individual awards gives a median gap of one day, because offices sign dozens of delivery orders together. Collapsing awards to account-days makes the interval mean something — and makes survival analysis on it defensible.

Provenance

Four tags, applied to every field.

Defined once in the pipeline and rendered into both the documentation and the console, so the two cannot disagree. Synthetic data never reaches the model or the ranking, and a synthetic reason code never becomes a recommended action — enforced by tests, not by convention.

REAL — straight from the source DERIVED — computed from real fields only SYNTHETIC — generated, never scored ASSUMPTION — a stated commercial input

24 invariant checks run with the pipeline and all 24 pass. If the model fails to beat its baseline, the baseline is kept and the console says so.

Install Base Reactivation Console. Built on US federal procurement data from USAspending.gov, public domain, with hardware failure rates from Backblaze drive statistics and margin benchmarks from SEC EDGAR filings. Accounts are federal awarding offices, not customers of any company.
